text_summary.body: Tattenai governor Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their companions asked who had decreed the building and the builders' names; the work continued until a report reached Darius. Their letter described the house of great stones and timber, quoted the elders: Nebuchadnezzar had destroyed the house; Cyrus in his first year decreed its rebuilding and gave the vessels to Sheshbazzar, whom he made governor and who laid the foundation; since then it had been building. They asked that the royal archives in Babylon be searched.

setting.period: Darius I's reign, after the resumption (c. 520–519 BC)
setting.body: "Beyond the River" (Akkadian Ebir-nāri) was the Persian province west of the Euphrates. A Babylonian document of 502 BC reportedly names a Tattannu governor of Ebir-nāri (Kidner via Guzik; Olmstead 1944, not read).

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik presents Tattenai as a fair administrator who preserved a copy of his letter, and notes the possible Babylonian attestation of his name and office (Kidner).
